ordered_diagnoses: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome

facts.raw_span: A 54-year-old man with glioblastoma
treated by surgical resection
began a clinical trial with M7824
a severely pruritic, nontender, erythematous papular and macular eruption
on his back, bilateral ankles, and upper extremities
no elevations in liver enzymes
no eosinophilia
no lymphadenopathy
the eruption represented a drug reaction to M7824
the rash progressed to grade III with worsening pruritus
M7824 infusions were held
prednisone at 40 mg per day was initiated

concepts.preferred_label: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome
aliases: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
concepts.why: The patient developed a severely pruritic, nontender, erythematous papular and macular eruption after starting M7824, which is consistent with a drug reaction, and the rash progressed despite initial treatment.
The patient's severe skin eruption, which progressed to grade III with worsening pruritus, is consistent with Stevens-Johnson syndrome, a severe skin and mucous membrane disorder.
The patient's severe skin eruption, which progressed to grade III with worsening pruritus, is consistent with toxic epidermal necrolysis, a severe skin condition.
The patient developed a severely pruritic, nontender, erythematous papular and macular eruption after starting M7824, which is consistent with an acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis.
The patient developed a maculopapular rash after starting M7824, which is a common type of drug reaction.

rationales.F06: The absence of liver enzyme elevations makes DRESS syndrome less likely.
rationales.F07: The absence of eosinophilia makes DRESS syndrome less likely.
rationales.F08: The absence of lymphadenopathy makes DRESS syndrome less likely.
rationales.F09: The eruption was classified as a drug reaction to M7824, which increases the likelihood of DRESS syndrome and other drug reactions.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of a severely pruritic, nontender, erythematous papular and macular eruption are consistent with a maculopapular rash, and there is no strong evidence to support a more specific diagnosis such as DRESS syndrome, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, or toxic epidermal necrolysis, which are often associated with additional systemic symptoms or laboratory findings not present in this case.
